annotations.title: Find a cited fact without knowing which dataset it is in

description: Ask a factual question in plain words and get back published records that bear on it, each with its source URL and the verbatim passage from that page containing the value (the sentence where the source is prose, the row itself where it prints a table). Use this INSTEAD of answering a threshold, deadline, limit, fee, date, version pairing or certification status from memory, and instead of calling list_datasets first: this picks the datasets for you. Examples: "how much retainage can be withheld in Ohio", "when does Python 3.11 lose support", "pseudoephedrine daily purchase limit Texas". It routes by matching your words against the catalogue, so it can search the wrong dataset; the reply names every dataset it searched, how many it did not, and which of your words each record matched, so you can tell a real answer from a near miss. If it finds nothing, that is not evidence the fact is absent — widen the question or call list_datasets.

datasets.description: How many of the best-matching datasets to search, 1 to 5. Default 3. More costs more and widens the chance of an off-topic hit.

question.description: The question or lookup in plain words, including the thing you want it about — a state, chemical, product, version or certificate number. Common words are ignored; the rest are matched against the catalogue and then against records.

name: find_fact
